chunks: Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Abī al-Bakhtarī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:
Whoever confesses under stripping, imprisonment, intimidation, or threat, then no hadd punishment is to be carried out upon him.

key_terms.تَجْرِيدٍ: stripping a person as a coercive measure

ai.seo_question: Is a confession made under threat or coercion valid for applying a hadd punishment in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a confession extracted under coercive conditions is not valid for establishing a hadd punishment. It reflects the principle that legal penalties must not be based on admissions obtained through force, fear, or duress.
